name: Bite reclamation

lead: Bite reclamation reopens a bite that has collapsed from tooth wear, such as from grinding or acid reflux, restoring the height of the lower face. Worn teeth can leave the lower face looking shortened, with the chin close to the nose.

Worn teeth are rebuilt so the jaws meet at a greater vertical dimension. It is described as part of complex full-mouth reconstruction involving many teeth; only brief encyclopedic descriptions were found, with no trials.

paras: It is large restorative dental work covering many teeth, usually planned and staged by a dentist. Temporaries or previews are often used to check appearance and bite.
Sources describe the work as complex, and no safety data specific to the procedure were found.

chain: Longer teeth and fuller lower face
angle.text: Those with teeth worn down by grinding or acid use bite reclamation to rebuild height, which can make the lower face look less shortened. Teeth are restored so the jaws meet higher, as part of full-mouth reconstruction.

lead: Bite reclamation is a term used in cosmetic dentistry for reopening the bite to restore vertical dimension lost through wear, such as from grinding or acid reflux, which can make the lower face look shortened [1]. It is described as part of full-mouth reconstruction, complex work involving many teeth [1].

Vertical dimension of occlusion is the up-and-down relationship of the jaws when the teeth meet, and dental references describe a deficient vertical dimension as giving a collapsed look with the chin close to the nose [2]. Sources found for this entry are encyclopedic summaries only; no published trial on bite reclamation was located.
infobox: Tooth wear from grinding or acid

paras: Cosmetic dentistry sources describe worn teeth reducing vertical dimension and bite reclamation restoring it [1]. Vertical dimension is assessed by facial proportion, speech sounds and rest position [2].
